'''Ernst Schmutzer''' (26 February 1930 – 20 February 2022) was a German [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]].<ref name=UniJenaES>{{cite web|url=http://www.physik.uni-jena.de/Fakult%C3%A4t/Historisches/Professoren+_+Galerie/20_+Jahrhundert/Schmutzer_+Ernst+%281930%29.html|title=Professoren - 20. Jahrhundert: Ernst Schmutzer|publisher=Physikalisch-Astronomische Fakultät, Friedrich-Schiller-Universität Jena|accessdate=28 March 2015|archive-date=2 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402153842/http://www.physik.uni-jena.de/Fakult%C3%A4t/Historisches/Professoren+_+Galerie/20_+Jahrhundert/Schmutzer_+Ernst+%281930%29.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=SudetanakadES>{{cite web| url=http://www.sudetendeutsche-akademie.eu/Schmutzer.htm| title=Prof. Dr. rer. nat. habil.Ernst Schmutzer| publisher=Sudetendeutsche Akademie der Wissenschaften und Künste e.V.| accessdate=28 March 2015| archive-date=2 April 2015| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402095806/http://www.sudetendeutsche-akademie.eu/Schmutzer.htm| url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenES>{{cite web |url=http://bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/wer-war-wer-in-der-ddr-%2363%3B-1424.html?ID=3101|author1=Dieter Hoffmann|title=Schmutzer, Ernst * 26.2.1930 Physiker|publisher= Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur: Biographische Datenbanken |language= German| accessdate= 28 March 2015}}</ref>

==Life==
===Early years===
{{more citations needed|date=July 2025}}
Ernst Schmutzer was born in 1930 in a small village in western [[Bohemia]], which at that time had been part of [[Czechoslovakia]] for slightly more than a decade. By May 1945, when the [[Second World War|war]] ended, he had attended schools in three different local villages. The area was occupied by the [[US army|Americans]] on 1 May 1945, and less than a year later the entire German speaking population [[Expulsion of Germans from Czechoslovakia|had been expelled]]. Schmutzer's schooling continued across the border in [[Weiden in der Oberpfalz|Weiden]]. By the time he passed his [[Abitur|school final exams]] in 1949<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenES/> he had been relocated again, this time to [[Waren (Müritz)]] in the northern part of what had at the time been designated the [[Soviet occupation zone]] in what remained of Germany. A few months later, in October 1949, the occupation zone was re-founded as the [[German Democratic Republic|German Democratic Republic (East Germany)]].

===Career progress===
He studied at the [[University of Rostock]], obtaining his first degree in 1953 and his doctorate just two years later. His dissertation,<ref>''Zur Theorie der Oberflächenspannung starker konzentrierter elektrolytischer Lösungen''</ref> for which he was supervised by [[Hans Falkenhagen]], concerned [[Electrolyte]]. After this, in 1955 he obtained a position as a research assistant at the [[University of Jena|Friedrich Schiller University of Jena]] which is where in 1958 he obtained his [[habilitation]] (a higher academic qualification).<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenES/> He obtained a lectureship at Jena in 1959 and in 1960 a professorship (with a teaching contract) in [[Theoretical physics]].<ref name=UniJenaES/> From 1968 till 1990 he was in charge of the "Relativistic Physics" field at Jena, serving between 1974 and 1978 as [[Dean (education)|Dean]] of the Mathematics, Natural Sciences and Engineering faculty. Between 1990 and his retirement in 1993 he was [[:de:Liste der Rektoren der Friedrich-Schiller-Universität Jena|Rector]] of Jena's [[University of Jena|Friedrich Schiller University]] in succession to Hans Schmigalla.<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenES/>

===Focus===
Schmutzer was concerned with the Theories of [[Theory of relativity|Relativity]] and [[Gravity|Gravitation]]. He investigated extensions of [[General relativity|General relativity theory]] in a supplementary [[Space|spatial dimension]] which he termed "Projective Unified Field Theory" (''"Projektive Einheitliche Feldtheorie"''), extrapolating from the ideas of [[Theodor Kaluza]].<ref>Those who had previously worked on similar ideas ("Projective Unified Field Theory") included, during the 1950s, [[Wolfgang Pauli]], [[Pascual Jordan]].</ref> This invokes five space-time dimensions including a massive supplementary [[scalar field]] which, according to Schmutzer, can serve as an explanation for the accelerating expansion of the universe identified in the 1990s (as a candidate for [[dark energy]]) and for the [[Pioneer anomaly|Pioneer effect]]. According to Schmutzer's theory the [[Gravitational singularity|singularities]] of [[General relativity|General relativity theory]] are smoothed, so that instead of a "Big bang" singularity, matter begins with a more gentle progression<ref name=UrstartES>{{cite web|url=http://www.rrp.infim.ro/2009_61_3/art05Schmu.pdf|title=OCCURRENCE OF AN ITERATIVE EXPONENTIAL FUNCTION IN COSMOLOGY WITHOUT THE BIG BANG SINGULARITY|work=Dedicated to Professor Ioan Gottlieb’s 80th anniversary|volume=Romanian Reports in Physics, Vol. 61, No. 3, P. 401–405, 2009|publisher=Editura Academiei Romane (Romanian Reports in Physics)|author=Ernst Schmutzer|date=4 June 2009|accessdate=29 March 2015|archive-date=2 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402170823/http://www.rrp.infim.ro/2009_61_3/art05Schmu.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> which Schmutzer termed an "Urstart".<ref name=DLRBerES>{{cite web|url=http://www.deutschlandradio.de/archiv/dlr/sendungen/zeitreisen/142660/index.html|author1=Rainer-Kurt Langner (interviewer)|author2=Ernst Schmutzer (interviewee)|title=Labor und Persönlichkeit: Der Physiker Ernst Schmutzer, Universität Jena|publisher=Deutschlandradio Berlin (subsequently renamed Deutschlandradio Kultur)|date=15 December 2001|accessdate=29 March 2015|archive-date=23 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923214024/http://www.deutschlandradio.de/archiv/dlr/sendungen/zeitreisen/142660/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Politics===
Politics was peripheral to Ernst Schmutzer's career, but in the [[German Democratic Republic]] it was hard to entirely ignore the country's ruling [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany#Basic organisation|Socialist Unity Party]].<ref name=JSabPanSED>{{cite web |url=http://www.bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/uploads/pdf-2010/pannen.pdf |title="Wo ein Genosse ist, da ist die Partei!"? - Stabilität und Erosion an der SED-Parteibasis |author=Sabine Pannen |publisher=Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur, Berlin |accessdate=23 March 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304101910/http://www.bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/uploads/pdf-2010/pannen.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> He joined the [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany|SED (party)]] in 1949, but was then expelled from it in 1958.<ref name=OliLemuES>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=44czKGuzLlgC&q=Ernst+Schmutzer+SED+1949&pg=PA1414|page=1414|title=Hochschule im Sozialismus: Studien zur Geschichte der Friedrich-Schiller=Universitaet Jena (1945-1990)|editor1=Uwe Hossfeld |editor2=Tobias Kaiser |editor3=Heinz Mestrup |work=Oliver Lemuth - Die Jenaer Hochschulphysik zwischen Entnazifizierung und "Dritte Hochschulreform" 1945 bis 1968|volume=1|publisher=[[:de:Böhlau Verlag|Böhlau Verlag]]|isbn=978-3-412-34505-1|date=2007|accessdate=29 March 2015}}</ref> The official report contained the conclusions that Schmutzer was in a fundamental disagreement with Party Policy regarding the practical transformation of the university. Following months of discussions in which Dr. Schmutzer had shown total disregard for party policy regarding scientific work, the conclusion was reached that his membership in the party could only be damaging to it, and he was expelled from the party.<ref name=OliLemuES/><ref>"[er] mit Grundfragen der Politik der Partei nicht einverstanden war (Praxis der Umgestaltung der Hochschule). Nach monatelangen Auseinandersetzungen mit Herrn Dr. Schmutzer, in denen sich insgesamt eine Geringschätzung der Politik gegenüber Wissenschaftlicher Arbeit zeigt, kam die Grundorganisation zur Auffassung, dass Dr. Schmutzer als Mitglied der Partei nur schädlich sein kann, deshalb erfolgte sein Ausschluss."</ref> Political exclusion turned out less damaging to Schmutzer's career than might have been anticipated.<ref name=OliLemuES/> He was one of just a handful of Jena professors permitted to visit western universities as a guest lecturer.<ref name=OliLemuES/> In 1967 he taught at [[Queen Mary University of London|Queen Mary College]] in [[London]].<ref name=OliLemuES/>

===International reputation===
Schmutzer became one of East Germany's leading theoretical physicists. An internationally recognised authority on [[Gravity|Gravitational Physics]], in 1979 he was able to celebrate [[Albert Einstein]]'s centenary by attracting to [[University of Jena|Jena]] the "9th International Conference on General Relativity and Gravitation" which took place in July 1980.<ref name=ISGRGES>{{cite web|url=http://www.isgrg.org/pastconfs.php|title=The GRn conferences|publisher=The International Society on General Relativity and Gravitation|accessdate=29 March 2015}}</ref> In Jena he created a School of Gravitation Physics, members of which include [[Hans Stephani]], Dietrich Kramer and Eduard Herlt, and which has established a name for itself, most notably, with investigation of precise solutions for the [[Einstein field equations]]. Between 1980 and 1990 he was a principal editor of the scientific journal "Experimentelle Technik der Physik".

==Awards, honours and memberships==
* 1969: Member [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]
* 1977: [[:de:Carus-Preis#Carus-Medaille|Carus Medal and Carus Prize from the city of Schweinfurt]] (awarded by the Leopoldina Academy)
* 1978: Service Medal from the [[Charles University in Prague]]
* 1981: [[National Prize of East Germany]]
* 1990: Corresponding Member [[German Academy of Sciences at Berlin]] (till 1992)
* 1990: Member [[:de:Akademie gemeinnütziger Wissenschaften zu Erfurt|Academy of Practical and Applied Sciences at Erfurt]]
* 1991: Member [[Saxonian Academy of Sciences and Humanities]]
* 1995: Member [[:de:Sudetendeutsche Akademie der Wissenschaften und Künste|Sudeten-German Academy of Arts and Sciences]]
* 2005: Name entered in the "Golden Book" of the [[Jena|City of Jena]]

In Jena Ernst Schmutzer was an honorary member of the [[:de:Burschenschaft Arminia auf dem Burgkeller|Burschenschaft Arminia auf dem Burgkeller]] ([[Arminius]] Student Fraternity of the City [hostelry] Cellar).
